architecture.mechanism: Bidirectional transformation via event sourcing applied to migration case data, enabling state reconstruction from an event log to verify and restore consistent system state.
architecture.intervention: Apply bidirectional event-sourcing traceability to the 2020 Hyundai Elantra ECU: log all sensor and CAN-bus events (throttle position, RPM, fuel trim, battery voltage, check-engine DTCs) to a persistent event store, then use a bidirectional transformation to reconcile the recorded event stream against the expected powertrain state model whenever a stall is reported, flagging the earliest event that violates state-consistency.
architecture.expected_effect: Intermittent power loss and sudden stalling become diagnosable post-hoc from stored DTCs and event logs, isolating the root-cause component (e.g., throttle body, crank/cam sensor, fuel pump, or battery voltage sag) without a physical teardown.
architecture.falsification_test: Replay the captured event stream of a stalling incident through the bidirectional transformation; if the reconstructed state matches the dealer-reported symptom timeline and the identified root-cause component is independently confirmed by a bench test or oscilloscope trace, the mechanism is supported — if reconstruction diverges or no consistent violating event is found, the mechanism is falsified for that incident.
